summary: - _(b) Take on record the Committee’s report dated 26.11.2025, which establishes the Petitioner’s diligence and confirms that the delay was for reasons not attributable to the Petitioner;_ - _(d) Pass any other order, further relief(s) in facts and circumstances of the case as this Hon'ble Commission may deem just and equitable in favor of the Petitioner._ - (h) CEA issued the “Approval for Energization” on 30.06.2025, confirming that the Petitioner’s infrastructure was complete and ready for commissioning on the originally scheduled date. - (k) The CTS was not fully commissioned by the extended date of 31.12.2025. The Petitioner submitted a further representation to the Committee on 03.02.2026. - (m) The Petitioner made additional submissions to the Committee on 18.02.2026 and 26.02.2026, detailing its generation readiness and the final commissioning status of the Project and requesting its approval for the extension in SCOD till the actual date of commissioning. - (a) The Petitioner filed a fresh representation before the Committee on 03.02.2026 along with additional submissions on 18.02.2026 and 26.02.2026, seeking a further extension up to 30.06.2026. - (c) The Petitioner successfully achieved commissioning on 24.02.2026, well within the timeline recommended under the second Committee report. In view of the above, this Commission may pass appropriate orders directing extension of the SCOD for the _ “The learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the present Petition has been filed inter alia seeking an extension of the Scheduled Commercial Operation Date (SCOD) of the Petitioner’s 50 MW Project from 30.6.2025 to 24.2.2026, the actual date of commissioning in order to retain the Project’s eligibility for the 100% waiver of ISTS charges. The learned counsel further submitted that the Committee constituted by the Commission, after detailed deliberations and examination of all documents and submissions, in its final report, has considered that the initial delay was not attributable to the Petitioner and recommended for grant of an extension of SCOD._ _ 2. After hearing the learned counsel for the Petitioner, the Commission directed as under: _ - _ (b) The Respondents to file their replies, if any, within three weeks with a copy to the Petitioner, who may file its rejoinder, if any, within two weeks thereafter. _ _ 3. The Petitioner is directed to clarify, on an affidavit, within two weeks, whether the project is being developed by M/s Avaada GJ Lakadia Pvt. Ltd. (AGPL)? If yes, relationship between AGPL and Petitioner?_ # ** Submissions of Petitioner in compliance with the RoP for hearing dated 30.04.2026: ** **5.** Petitioner vide affidavit dated 20.5.2026 and 21.05.2026 submitted that the 50 MW Solar Power Project, which is the subject matter of the present Petition, is being developed through AGPL, which was formerly a wholly owned subsidiary of the Petitioner. However, as on date, both AGPL and the Petitioner are wholly owned subsidiaries of Avaada Energy Private Limited (AEPL), the parent company being the same for both entities. **6.** The connectivity was granted to the Petitioner, and applications before the Committee for extension in SCOD and waiver were made by the Petitioner on behalf of AGPL. _ “The learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the present Petition has been filed inter alia seeking an extension of the Scheduled Commercial Operation Date (SCOD) of the Petitioner’s 50 MW Solar Power Project from 30.6.2025 to 24.2.2026 for the purpose of retaining the eligibility for waiver of ISTS charges. The learned counsel further submitted that the Committee, constituted under the Sharing Regulations, has also, vide Reports dated 26.11.2025 and 11.3.2026, recommended for extension of SCOD up to 30.6.2026 or until the date of actual commissioning of the necessary CTS, whichever is earlier. The learned counsel further submitted that the Petitioner has filed the ROP compliance affidavit on 21.5.2026, clarifying that the 50 MW Solar Power Project is being developed through Avaada GJ Lakadia Private Limited/AGPL, which was formerly a wholly owned subsidiary of the Petitioner. However, as on date, both AGPL and the Petitioner are wholly owned subsidiaries of Avaada Energy Private Limited (AEPL), the parent company being the same for both entities. The learned counsel further submitted that the 2nd proviso to Regulation 15.1 of GNA Regulations permits the utilisation of connectivity granted to a subsidiary company of a Parent company by other subsidiary company(ies). The learned counsel also sought liberty to file a brief affidavit and requested that the matter be reserved for order._ _ 2. The learned counsel for the Respondent/CTUIL submitted that CTUIL has also filed its compliance affidavit in terms of ROP dated 30.4.2025, and that the Connectivity of 50 MW granted to the Petitioner has been made effective from 28.3.2026._ _ 3. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsels for the parties, the Commission permitted the Petitioner to file its affidavit within a week and subject to this, the matter was reserved for order.” _ **10.** We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner and the Respondent, and the documents placed on the record. The following issue arises for our consideration: _ On the basis of the material on record, and having regard to Regulation and the Commission's Office Order dated 30.07.2025, the Committee recommends to the Hon'ble Commission as follows:_ **18.** In view of the above discussions, we are of the considered view that SCOD of the Petitioner stands extended to 24.2.2026, only for the purpose of Regulation 13(2) (h) of the Sharing Regulations and not otherwise, and the Petitioner’s project shall be eligible for waiver of inter-state transmission charges, as if the project had achieved
